content.value_statement: Medical device teams need consistent ISO 14971 risk files across design, verification, and post-market work. This skill guides risk analysis, controls, documentation, and lifecycle updates.
actual_capabilities: Guides ISO 14971 risk management planning and file maintenance.
Helps identify hazards, hazardous situations, foreseeable misuse, and use errors.
Supports risk estimation, acceptability decisions, and residual risk review.
Recommends risk control measures and verification documentation.
Connects risk work with IEC 62304, cybersecurity, QMS, and regulatory submission workflows.
limitations: Does not replace qualified regulatory, clinical, or legal review.
Does not provide validated medical device templates; included support files are placeholders.
Does not calculate risk automatically without user-provided criteria and data.
Requires device context, hazards, controls, evidence, and acceptability criteria from the user.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Risk Management Plan
use_cases.description: Draft a plan structure with scope, responsibilities, acceptability criteria, deliverables, and review cadence.

use_cases.title: Analyze Software Safety Risks
use_cases.description: Connect software hazards, failure modes, risk controls, and IEC 62304 safety classification decisions.

use_cases.title: Maintain Post-Market Risk Files
use_cases.description: Review complaints, surveillance signals, control effectiveness, and risk file update needs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Plan Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ISO 14971 risk management plan outline for a Class II device. Include scope, roles, criteria, deliverables, and review cadence.

prompt_templates.title: Review Hazard Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these device functions and intended users. Identify likely hazards, hazardous situations, foreseeable misuse, and missing risk analysis inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Map Controls to Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Map each unacceptable risk to control options, residual risk checks, verification evidence, and risk-benefit documentation needs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Risk File
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this risk management file for ISO 14971 completeness. Flag missing traceability, weak acceptability rationale, and post-production update gaps.

output_examples.input: A team needs a risk management plan for a connected infusion device.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a plan outline covering scope, team roles, criteria, cybersecurity interfaces, deliverables, and scheduled file reviews.

output_examples.input: A software team lists alarm failure, incorrect dose calculation, and data loss hazards.
output_examples.output: The skill organizes hazardous situations, estimates risk inputs, suggests control categories, and identifies verification evidence for each risk.

output_examples.input: A quality team has complaint trends and wants to update the risk file.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a post-market review path, including signal evaluation, residual risk review, control effectiveness checks, and documentation updates.

best_practices: Provide device type, intended use, user groups, environment, and known hazards.
Share your risk matrix, acceptability criteria, and existing control hierarchy.
Ask for traceability between hazards, controls, verification, residual risk, and post-market evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated content as approved regulatory documentation.
Do not omit clinical evidence, complaint data, or usability findings from risk reviews.
Do not ask for final risk acceptability decisions without defined criteria and accountable reviewers.

faq.question: What standard does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on ISO 14971 risk management for medical devices across the product lifecycle.

faq.question: Can it help with software risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can connect software hazards and controls with IEC 62304 risk management activities.

faq.question: Does it create validated regulatory documents?
faq.answer: No. It creates guidance and draft structures that qualified teams must review and approve.

faq.question: What inputs improve the results?
faq.answer: Provide device context, intended use, hazards, risk criteria, existing controls, and verification evidence.

faq.question: Can it support post-market risk updates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide complaint trend review, surveillance signal evaluation, and risk file update planning.

faq.question: Is it only for regulatory teams?
faq.answer: No. Quality, engineering, clinical, cybersecurity, and software teams can use it for risk work.
